# Retained results and unfinished earlier claims

<!-- Generated by tools/roadmap-status.py --write; edit the catalog and renderer. -->

The active [roadmap](../PLAN.md) focuses on refactoring, targeted code changes and Lean proof writing for smaller agents. This page audits the earlier qualification checklist and its original acceptance conditions. It preserves unfinished claims without treating them as current roadmap milestones.

For example, a checkout repair should find the calculation and callers, explain the bug, produce a reviewed patch and pass the test that catches the rounding error. Finding the function is useful, but it does not establish that whole outcome.

**15 of 18 specific test requirements have matching recorded results; 3 remain open. 1 of 4 earlier goals are complete.** These counts do not measure product readiness or savings for an agent.

A requirement is one specific behavior we promise to check. A recorded result describes a chosen program, inputs and tool revision. “Demonstrated” means that result meets its stated requirement; “open” means required work or matching results are missing.

## What works and what still gets in the way

| User task | What we have now | What remains |
|---|---|---|
| Find the code behind a bug | Function locations, known callers and selected source reads | Reliable explanations on unfamiliar tasks with less wasted reading |
| Trace input to an output | Selected original-package questions in Boltons, dateutil, JDcal and Stringcase, including number, date and text values | Other imports and unsupported behavior still leave many answers incomplete |
| Continue after a failed attempt | Saved answers match fresh checks through seven changes on three projects | Complete session costs are recorded; agent benefits need separate live results |
| Deliver a repair or check a property | Real Rust and Python renames, including behavior checks, undo and patch replay | Independent agent task success and a checked connection between proofs and actual code |

**We have not demonstrated general time or cost savings.** The older two-task comparison used more calls, reading and time with fr than with ordinary file tools. The recent Python repository scripts apply known repairs; they test editing and recovery. They do not measure an agent discovering the repair. The [measurement guide](benchmarks.md) explains baselines, included costs and unmeasured overhead. Read the [product review](product-review.md) and [result meanings](understanding-results.md).

## Active work follows the focused roadmap

The active roadmap focuses on smaller agents refactoring code, making targeted changes and writing Lean proofs. [M1](../PLAN.md#m1-run-the-selected-agents-on-three-complete-tasks) has [thirty-six recorded attempts](../tests/agent-eval/selected-agents/local-results/README.md) on a rename, Unicode repair and Lean proof, including failures and observed overhead. [M2](../PLAN.md#m2-make-multi-file-refactorings-and-targeted-changes-dependable) checks specific Rust, Python and TypeScript changes, preserved source and complete delivery. [M3](../PLAN.md#m3-help-the-agents-write-repair-and-maintain-lean-proofs) checks the agent proof-writing loop, Boolean language cases and numeric properties. [M2 results](../tests/agent-eval/project-edits/local-results/README.md) retain all 48 attempts: 43 finished with correct patches and five timed out. Every selected agent has an accepted result per task using fr. M3 is next. This report retains the earlier qualification conditions; its counts do not measure completion of the focused roadmap.

See the [plan](../PLAN.md#next-work) for the work sequence and [generalization requirements](../PLAN.md#generalization-requirements) for the testing policy.

## Original finite acceptance obligations

These are the specific requirements, checked one by one. Each item gives a user example, what must be established, its recorded results and the remaining action under that earlier scope. IDs such as `B.contract` let tests refer to the same requirement; readers can follow the accompanying question.

An oracle is an independent reference check, such as Python execution. A source binding records fingerprints of inputs behind a saved result. Changed inputs require renewed checks. A held-out project stays unread while developing the tool, then tests whether the rules work beyond familiar examples.

A source supplies a tracked input; a sink consumes it. A sanitizer is a user-declared cleaning function for a particular output context, such as HTML. An effect is another action the code performs, such as writing a file.

A cache saves earlier results for possible reuse. Reuse must check their recorded inputs before trusting them. Latency means elapsed request time; aggregate memory measures the combined memory held by the measured processes.

### A.exact: Point to the exact code behind an answer

User example: An agent explains a bug and links the exact call and source lines it inspected.

**State: demonstrated.** Nine small Python tests check the reported source locations, including repeated calls and missing information; no unsupported fact may be reported as established.

Recorded results or remaining work: [exact-facts](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-26-m2-current-flow-facts/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: Keep these location tests passing as discovery changes.

### A.repositories: Deliver the two recorded example changes

User example: Replay the two prescribed repository repairs and check their behavior, saved changes and delivery.

**State: demonstrated.** The recorded boltons bug fix and more-itertools feature pass their independent behavior tests and can be applied again in a separate checkout. These scripts already contain the intended edits.

Recorded results or remaining work: [repository-tasks](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-26-m2-current-python-repositories/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: Keep these delivery regression tests; evaluate unscripted problem solving separately.

### A.live-repeat: Measure whether agents actually work better with fr

User example: Compare agents fixing the same unfamiliar bug, counting all work including failed attempts.

**State: open.** Run the 48-attempt pilot defined in the product review: two model families, ordinary tools versus fr, repeated tasks, and a separate delegated-task comparison. Retain failures and account for all agents, cache usage, time and cost. Report quality and efficiency separately, including inconclusive or negative results.

Recorded results or remaining work: No saved result yet meets this requirement.

Earlier requirement still needs: R4: agree exact models, settings, prices and spending caps. Finish the prepared eighteen-attempt comparison, then the separate 48-attempt study. Count setup, retries, failed attempts, every child agent and complete resource use; preserve unknown billing.

### A.compiler-profile: Relate explanations to compiler and runtime checks

User example: A Rust expression parses, but the selected build reports a type error at that expression.

**State: demonstrated.** For the declared Rust and Python language features, record build inputs and versions, disagreements with fr, repeated calls on one line, shadowed names and Unicode positions. Check both correct answers and explicit unsupported cases.

Recorded results or remaining work: [compiler-profile](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-26-m2-current-compiler-profile/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: Keep the declared profile and ambiguity refusals passing; specify reusable Python behavior in B.contract.

### B.scalar: Trace simple values through package helpers

User example: Follow an input through a simple helper and check whether overwriting the value removes the original connection.

**State: demonstrated.** The existing small package tests correctly report a value reaching a selected use and a value blocked by a context-appropriate sanitizer; both analyses finish with zero false claims.

Recorded results or remaining work: [package-flow](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-26-m2-current-package-flow/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: Keep the small examples as regression tests while testing more varied programs.

### B.contract: Specify reusable Python behavior

User example: A helper returns its left argument; check selected, ignored and overwritten input cases against Python.

**State: demonstrated.** Document how evaluation order, assignments, function calls, exceptions and source locations are represented. For every supported construct, compare fr with Python execution across independently authored examples and renamed or relocated equivalents. Identify unsupported constructs explicitly. No repository identity or expected answer may select semantics.

Recorded results or remaining work: [python-contract](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-26-m2-current-python-contract/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: R1 adds base-ten integer conversion errors and caught error objects to the bounds form. R2 adds shared-list writes through helpers. Compare each reusable rule with independent Python results and renamed or moved examples. Preserve explicit incomplete answers, limits and fresh recorded inputs.

### B.repository-flow: Trace values in unfamiliar projects

User example: Trace an input through a real imported library without mistaking an unfinished answer for safety.

**State: demonstrated.** With one unchanged analyzer, test a value that reaches a selected use and one that cannot reach it on at least three independently selected Python repositories, including one held out until implementation is frozen. Runtime checks and independent inspection must agree. Rename and relocate supported examples without changing results. Unknown effects or exhausted budgets must prevent a no-path claim.

Recorded results or remaining work: [original-package-questions](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-26-m2-current-text-package-recheck/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: R2 rechecks Toolz return_none, Funcy inc and dec, and Pydash add through their original imports. Record each remaining startup obstacle. Reserve a new independent project before reading its implementation, freeze the checking procedure and preserve its first attempt.

### B.effects: Handle exceptions and shared mutable values honestly

User example: A helper mutates a shared list; the answer must account for later reads of that same object.

**State: demonstrated.** Independent Python examples cover explicit raise, implicit exceptions, handlers and two names referring to the same object. Report exact locations and distinguish supported behavior from behavior the analyzer cannot determine.

Recorded results or remaining work: [python-effects](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-25-m2-current-python-effects/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: Keep the original-import error-handler repair and exact unchecked-effect locations passing. Choose a concrete project change that needs implicit errors or shared mutable values, then add reusable rules and independent behavior checks.

User example: Measure whether saved answers reduce total work and storage on a real project after edits.

**State: demonstrated.** On at least three independently selected projects, including a held-out project, repeat first-run, cached and single-edit analysis three times. Record latency, aggregate memory, disk growth, text delivered to the agent, work repeated and agreement with a fresh analysis.

User example: Apply a reviewed repair, run its required checks and verify the exported patch in another checkout.

**State: demonstrated.** The two recorded example changes pass their behavior checks, undo and redo correctly, and pass again when their exported patch is applied in a separate checkout. Saved completion records identify what was checked.

Recorded results or remaining work: [repository-tasks](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-26-m2-current-python-repositories/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: Keep these behavior and patch-replay tests passing.

### D.structural: Change a declaration and update its callers

User example: Rename Boltons' `clamp` function to `clamp_value` and update its callers and documentation. Limiting 70 to the range 0 through 50 must still return 50.

**State: demonstrated.** Complete one Rust and one Python rename or signature-change task, including affected callers, configuration and tests. Compile or execute the changed program, undo the change and replay its patch in another checkout.

Recorded results or remaining work: [current-project-changes](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-26-m2-current-project-changes-recheck/result.json).

### D.translation: Translate a function without changing its promised behavior

User example: Move a small helper to another language and check its promised inputs, outputs and error behavior.

**State: demonstrated.** Translate one pure function between Rust and Python with integer arithmetic and branches. Specify input ranges, overflow, errors and evaluation order. Independently compare every input in a bounded range and the declared boundary cases.

Recorded results or remaining work: [checked-translation](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-25-m2-current-checked-translation/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: Keep exact integer division, operand evaluation order and the independent bounded checks passing. Other functions and input domains need their own contracts and checks.

### D.existing-proof: Connect a proof to the existing code it describes

User example: Check that a proof of an access rule describes the actual function and its language behavior.

**State: open.** For one existing function, retain the property, mathematical model, old and new code, and a checked argument connecting the implementation to the model. A relevant source edit must invalidate the proof claim.

Recorded results or remaining work: No saved result yet meets this requirement.

Earlier requirement still needs: R3 connects the existing page_count implementation to its signed-64-bit contract and Lean proof. Deliberately wrong comparisons, results and dependencies must expire saved claims and reject fresh proof attempts. A separate model theorem cannot close this item.

### D.new-proof: Write new code together with a checked specification

User example: Write a new access function together with its required rule and a checked proof of that rule.

**State: open.** For one new function, write its specification and implementation together, check their connection between the descriptions and Lean proof, run behavior tests and replay delivery in a separate checkout. Identify all trusted components.

Recorded results or remaining work: No saved result yet meets this requirement.

Earlier requirement still needs: R3 specifies and implements fits_window(offset, count, total) over unsigned 64-bit inputs. An empty range at the end is valid; a range past the end is invalid. Connect the actual subtraction-based implementation to its proof, test altered claims and replay delivery independently.

### D.host: Recover safely when an edit process is interrupted

User example: Resume or undo an interrupted edit without overwriting someone else’s newer work.

**State: demonstrated.** The native recovery tests interrupt the edit process at the declared journal checkpoints and exercise all 224 small decision-model cases. This does not establish recovery after power loss.

Recorded results or remaining work: [host-recovery](../tests/agent-eval/results/2026-10-26-m2-current-host-recovery/result.json).

Earlier requirement still needs: Keep the process-interruption tests passing and preserve the limit on what they establish.

## Limits and interpretation

- These records retain the earlier qualification checklist and its original acceptance conditions. The active roadmap focuses on smaller agents doing refactoring, targeted code changes and Lean proof writing. Earlier counts do not establish completion of those new milestones.
- The analyzer and SDK must not branch on benchmark repository names, paths, revisions or expected patches. Explicit user rules may select sources and uses; they cannot bypass language semantics or unsupported effects.
- Demonstrated items retain their finite scope. Broader requirements need unfamiliar projects, independent language examples and complete agent-cost accounting.
- The existing agent comparison used an older Luna model on two Rust tasks. The fr runs consumed more calls, context and time. There is no established general token or cost advantage, and no matched Sonnet or delegated-agent result here.
- Current evidence means the recorded input hashes still match. It does not establish that every dependency was recorded; the independent behavior checks must also run.
- Parsing a language does not imply full analysis or editing support. Dynamic imports, package initialization effects, runtime dispatch, merging namespace packages from multiple roots and wildcard export insertion remain limits of the current Python analysis or writer.
- A proof about a model, a correct source location and a passing runtime test establish different things. Proofs about the source implementation require an explicit checked connection.
- Saved findings about source code cannot track reStructuredText (RST) files directly. Boltons' documentation uses an exact text replacement with a saved review, undo and an explicit check of every named Python object. The earlier more-itertools task used an unchanged Python module as its independent observation.

Evidence baseline: `cdc17dca7ce2564cb21a1e7077e38c7cab572712`. Acceptance requirements: `agent-analysis-v2`.

Run `python3 tools/roadmap-status.py --check` to detect report drift, `--write` to regenerate both reports after reviewing changes, or `--require-complete` to require all earlier qualification tests and implementation items.
